bull.b: The 20-year PPA secures a substantial power supply for Phase 1, addressing a critical requirement for data-center development. Long-duration contracted access can improve project bankability, support tenant commitments, and reduce exposure to future power availability constraints.

bull.t: Permitted project with cost-efficient development plan
bull.b: Permitting completion and active site work indicate that Phase 1 has progressed beyond an early concept. The modular approach and targeted cost advantage could improve capital efficiency, shorten commissioning, and support stronger project economics if execution remains on schedule.

The PIPE and reported cash position provide resources to advance leasing and development while reducing near-term debt pressure. A stronger funding base can improve negotiating flexibility with tenants and financing partners as the company works to convert its project pipeline into operating assets.

bear.t: Severe revenue decline and continuing cash burn
bear.b: The collapse in revenue and deeply negative profitability show that the existing operating base is not yet generating durable earnings. Persistent negative operating cash flow and free cash flow require continued external funding, limiting financial flexibility and increasing execution pressure.

bear.t: Phase 1 lease and project financing remain incomplete
bear.b: A non-executed lease leaves the central customer commitment unresolved and prevents the project’s economics from being fully locked in. Until lease terms, funding, and delivery obligations are finalized, construction timing, capital needs, and the path to recurring revenue remain uncertain.

Regulatory delays could extend development schedules and defer the company’s transition from development spending to operating revenue. Pending approvals also complicate equipment, financing, and tenant planning, while prolonged uncertainty could increase execution costs across the Texas project.
